questions.stem: Given the recurrence relation T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n^2, what is the time complexity using the Master Theorem?
questions.solution: The recurrence relation can be written in the form T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n), where a = 4, b = 2, and f(n) = n^2. Since f(n) = O(n^2) and n^2 is in Θ(n^(log_24)), which is Θ(n^2), we can apply the Master Theorem Case 2. This case states that if a > b^k (where k is the exponent of f(n) / (n^(log_24))), then T(n) = Θ(n^(log_24) * n^2 / n^(log_24)) = Θ(n^2). Therefore, the time complexity is O(n^2).
questions.explanation: The Master Theorem helps analyze divide- and-conquer algorithms by classifying recurrence relations into three cases. Case 1 applies when f(n) is smaller than n^(log_ba), Case 2 when f(n) is in Θ(n^(log_ba)), and Case 3 when f(n) is larger. In this case, we are in Case 2.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose A (O(n)) because it might seem like the linear term n^2 dominates. However, according to the Master Theorem, the dominant factor comes from the recursive calls, which leads to a quadratic time complexity.
